The iPhone Ultra launch event is just weeks away, but new reports suggest that initial supply may be extremely limited, and the phone may only be available in the United States when it goes on sale.

iPhone Ultra supply is tight; initial launch may be exclusive to the United States

Apple will hold an event in the United States on 8 September, when it will unveil its first foldable iPhone — but it will not go on sale immediately. A major Chinese component supplier has confirmed that Apple is facing challenges in supply, testing, and pricing, which could mean the Australian market will have to wait several months before seeing the device. The supplier told ChannelNews that the delay is "mainly due to supply and pricing issues," and added: "We believe Apple is also having difficulties with prototype testing." Australian telecoms operators and a major retailer have confirmed that this "Apple Fold" will not appear on local retail shelves this time. Due to limited supply, the product will launch first in the United States before expanding to other major markets including China.

We have heard rumours before that iPhone Ultra supply could be very tight at launch. If this turns out to be true, launching first in the United States as a short-term measure is also a reasonable approach.

Although this report sounds plausible, there is reason to remain sceptical.

First, the report mentions an event on 8 September, but Apple will almost certainly not choose that date.

Choosing the second Tuesday for an event has always been a safe choice, but this year the US Labor Day falls slightly later, on 7 September. It would be extremely unwise for Apple to hold an iPhone launch event the day after Labor Day. Wednesday 9 September is actually more likely.

In addition, the sources for this report seem to come from China and Australia. If the iPhone Ultra will not be launching in these regions in the short term, it is reasonable for local insiders to know in advance. But they may not know whether the device will be exclusively available in the United States at launch — that claim looks more like speculation.

In any case, it would not be surprising for Apple to roll out the iPhone Ultra gradually. If it can ship in the United States in September and then gradually add more markets, that is better than delaying the entire launch event.

When do you expect to get your hands on the iPhone Ultra? Let us know in the comments.
